record.context_brief: Existence of nonquadratic full-domain right D-Chebyshev geometry
record.original_question: Does there exist a Legendre function f: R^n -> [-infinity, +infinity] with full domain X = R^n such that f is not quadratic, yet every nonempty closed convex subset of X is right D-Chebyshev with respect to the Bregman distance induced by f? Equivalently, can there be a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre function whose gradient map grad f is nonaffine but still preserves convexity in the strong sense needed for every nonempty closed convex subset of X to have a unique right Bregman nearest point from each x in U?

evidence.quote: Fact 3.4 (See [6, Lemma 3.5].) Suppose that f is the negative entropy (see Example 1.1(ii)) and that C is convex. Then C is ->D-Chebyshev.

Fact 3.4 raises two intriguing questions. Apart from the case of quadratic functions, are there instances of f where f has full domain and where every closed convex subset of U is ->D-Chebyshev? Because of Fact 3.2, an affirmative answer to this question would imply that grad f is a (quite surprising) nonaffine yet convexity-preserving transformation.

Problem 3. Does there exist a Legendre function f with full domain such that f is not quadratic yet every nonempty closed convex subset of X is ->D-Chebyshev? In view of Fact 3.1, the gradient operator grad f of such a function would be nonaffine and it would preserve convexity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ge 2$. A proper lower semicontinuous convex function $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to (-\infty,+\infty]$ is called a Legendre function if it is essentially smooth (differentiable on the nonempty interior $U = \mathrm{int}(\mathrm{dom}\,f)$ with $\|\nabla f(x_k)\| \to \infty$ whenever $x_k \to x \in \mathrm{bdry}(\mathrm{dom}\,f)$) and essentially strictly convex (strictly convex on every convex subset of $\mathrm{dom}\,\partial f$). Assume $f$ has full domain, i.e. $\mathrm{dom}\,f = \mathbb{R}^n$, so $U = \mathbb{R}^n$. The Bregman distance induced by $f$ is
$$D_f(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - \langle \nabla f(y),\, x-y\rangle, \qquad x,y \in \mathbb{R}^n.$$
A nonempty closed set $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is called right $D$-Chebyshev (with respect to $f$) if for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ the problem $\min_{c \in C} D_f(x,c)$ has a unique minimizer.

Question: Does there exist a Legendre function $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ with full domain $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that
(i) $f$ is not a quadratic function (equivalently, $\nabla f$ is not affine), and
(ii) every nonempty closed convex subset $C$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is right $D$-Chebyshev?
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent work by Bauschke, Lucet, and Trienis ("Legendre Functions Whose Gradients Map Convex Sets to Convex Sets") establishes that on a Banach space of dimension at least two, a differentiable function with continuous, one-to-one gradient that maps convex sets to convex sets must have an affine gradient. Since an affirmative answer to the problem would force $\nabla f$ to be a continuous, one-to-one, convexity-preserving (yet nonaffine) map, this result rules out such an $f$ in dimension $\ge 2$, resolving the question in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Legendre Functions Whose Gradients Map Convex Sets to Convex Sets
status_evidence.snippet: A differentiable function on a Banach space of dimension at least two has an affine gradient provided the gradient is continuous and one-to-one and maps convex sets to convex sets.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous one-to-one gradients that preserve convexity must be affine in dimension >= 2, which together with the Bregman/Chebyshev framework precludes a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre function with every closed convex set right D-Chebyshev.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances and Chebyshev sets (Bauschke-Macklem-Sewell-Wang)
status_evidence.snippet: An affirmative answer to this question would imply that grad f is a (quite surprising) nonaffine yet convexity-preserving transformation.
status_evidence.claim: The original problem is equivalent to the existence of a nonaffine convexity-preserving gradient of a Legendre function with full domain.
